Pregnancy Due Date Finder

A pregnancy due date finder estimates your baby’s expected delivery date (EDD) and current gestational age based on the first day of your Last Menstrual Period (LMP), conception date, or ultrasound date. Using clinical Naegele’s rule (280 days / 40 weeks from LMP), it generates an organized trimester timeline and developmental milestones.

Formula and Calculation Method

Standard Naegele’s Rule for Estimated Date of Delivery (EDD):

EDD = First day of LMP + 1 year - 3 months + 7 days
Or: EDD = First day of LMP + 280 days (40 full gestational weeks)
Conception Date Method: EDD = Date of Conception + 266 days (38 weeks)

Trimester Breakdown: First Trimester (Weeks 1–13), Second Trimester (Weeks 14–27), Third Trimester (Weeks 28–40+).

Worked Example and Step-by-Step Calculation

Due Date from Last Menstrual Period (LMP on April 10, 2026)
Input Values:
  • Calculation Method: Last Menstrual Period (LMP)
  • First Day of LMP: April 10, 2026
  • Average Cycle Length: 28 days

1. Add 7 days to day of LMP: April 10 + 7 days = April 17

2. Subtract 3 months: April - 3 months = January

3. Advance 1 year: 2026 + 1 = 2027

4. Estimated Date of Delivery (EDD) = January 15, 2027

5. End of 1st Trimester: July 10, 2026 (13 weeks)

6. End of 2nd Trimester: October 16, 2026 (27 weeks)

Result: Estimated Due Date: January 15, 2027 (Full 40 Gestational Weeks)

How to Use the Pregnancy Due Date Finder

  1. Select your calculation basis: Last Menstrual Period (LMP), Conception Date, or IVF Transfer Date.
  2. Enter the corresponding date and your typical menstrual cycle length (default 28 days).
  3. Instantly view your estimated delivery date and current gestational progress (weeks + days).
  4. Review your comprehensive pregnancy calendar mapping trimesters and key clinical screening windows.

Common Mistakes, Limitations & Practical Guidance

  • Only about 4% to 5% of babies arrive precisely on their calculated due date; full-term birth normally occurs between 37 and 42 weeks.
  • First-trimester crown-rump length (CRL) ultrasound measurements provide the most clinically authoritative dating if menstrual dates are irregular.

Frequently Asked Questions About Pregnancy Due Date Finder

How accurate is a pregnancy due date calculator?

Calculations based on Naegele’s rule provide an estimated benchmark. While only ~4% of births occur on the exact date, approximately 80% of babies are born within two weeks before or after the estimated date (between 38 and 42 weeks of gestation).

Why is gestational age calculated from the last period instead of conception?

Because most women know the date their period started, but pinpointing the exact day of ovulation and conception is biologically difficult. Consequently, obstetricians measure gestational age from the first day of the last menstrual period, making pregnancy ~40 weeks long even though the fetus is ~38 weeks old.

How does cycle length affect the due date calculation?

Naegele’s rule assumes a standard 28-day cycle with ovulation on day 14. If your average cycle is 32 days, ovulation likely occurred around day 18, so your due date shifts forward by 4 days.

When does each trimester begin and end?

The first trimester spans from conception through week 13. The second trimester spans weeks 14 through 27. The third trimester begins at week 28 and continues until delivery.

What is considered a full-term pregnancy?

The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) defines full term as delivery between 39 weeks 0 days and 40 weeks 6 days, when infant organ development is optimal.
